2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec9::child0
citations.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

citations.chunk_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

To further verify the superiority of N-TEP/G2 electrolyte, high-mass loading PB||HC full cells are assembled (Fig. 5a). The N-TEP/G2 based full cell maintains a stable cycling performance at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ $(1.0\mathrm{C} = 150\mathrm{mA})$

$g^{-1}$ ), delivering the high capacity of 98.7 mAh $g^{-1}$ after 300 cycles with capacity retention of 83.1 %. In sharp contrast, much lower capacity of 79.7 mAh $g^{-1}$ and capacity retention of 68.7 % are realized in N-TEP electrolyte (Fig. 5b and c). As shown in Fig. 5d, PB||HC full cell with N-TEP/G2 electrolyte delivers discharge capacities of 127.6, 121.5, 113.8, 105.6, and 87.1 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.2 C, 0.5 C, 0.8 C, 1.0 C, and 1.5 C, much higher than that of 127.7, 116.0, 99.3, 86.9, and 65.8 mAh $g^{-1}$ with N-TEP electrolyte. Corresponding charge-discharge profiles are presented in Fig. S22, where the N-TEP/G2 system consistently exhibits lower overpotentials and higher capacity retention across all current densities. citations.quote:
Ronnie Mogensen, Alexander Buckel, Simon Colbin, and Reza Younesi\*

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

Cite This: Chem. Mater. 2021, 33, 1130–1139

Read Online

ACCESS |

Metrics & More

Article Recommendations

SI Supporting Information

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures. Full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes were evaluated at room temperature and 55 °C using the aforementioned electrolytes. The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. The flammability tests indicate that NaBOB in NMP-TMP electrolytes are nonflammable when the electrolyte contains more than 30 vol % TMP.

NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. The studied electrolytes provided promising long-term cycling in full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes. NaBOB–NMP–TMP electrolytes containing less than 30 vol % NMP are nonflammable and share properties like good ionic conductivity over a wide temperature range while possessing good high-temperature performance and retaining over 50% capacity over 1000 cycles.

![](images/02b845ef0cc752ae9cb076145efdcf41689eb321b41ae3285eab9d31cbe0e36b.jpg)  
Figure 10. Radar plot comparing TMP–NaBOB, NMP–NaBOB, and TMP–NMP 1:1 NaBOB electrolytes. The figure shows ionic conductivity. Freezing point as determined using the $0.1 \, mS cm^{-1}$ temperature as a threshold. Rate capability is described as the percent remaining capacity in the first discharge at 8C as compared to the initial discharge capacity. Cycling stability and high-temperature performance likewise compare the initial discharge capacity with the capacity at cycles 1000 and 100, respectively.

The nature of this passivation is unknown, although studies on LiBOB suggest that formation of AlBO $_{3}$ occurs concurrently with electrolyte oxidation in EC:DMC 1 M LiBOB electrolytes. $^{34}$

Electrochemical Cycling. To test the viability of the NMP-TMP solvent mixtures with NaBOB salt as the electrolyte system in sodium-ion batteries, we used full cells with hard carbon (HC) anodes and Prussian white (PW) cathodes. Initial cycling was performed at $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (0.2C) for five cycles; after this, cycling progressed at $150\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (1C) until cycle 52 where a $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ current was used for a single cycle to ascertain the amount of capacity recovery at low current. All the reported capacities and C-rates are calculated from the active material weight of the cathode assuming $150\ mAh\cdot g^{-1}$ capacity. $^{35}$ Note that a minimum of three cells was cycled for each electrolyte formulation to present the variance in the measurements. During the first formation cycle at 0.2C, the cells with NaBOB–TMP achieved 73% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) while the corresponding value for NaBOB–NMP was 68%. These values can be compared to the 83% CE of the first cycle for the cells using 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC, which is included here as a reference.

citations.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

evidence_ledger.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

evidence_ledger.quote: This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries. Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. Compared with the commonly used ether solvents, TEP endows the lower HOMO energy level, indicating its excellent antioxidant ability; however, it tends to preferentially decompose at anode surface due to its much lower LUMO energy level, forming the unstable TEP-based solid electrolyte interface (SEI). Moreover, the charge densities of atoms are simulated by electrostatic potential (ESP) density distributions in Fig. 1c, where electrophilic sites mainly concentrated on oxygen atoms and nucleophilic sites on hydrogen atoms [31]. In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

evidence_ledger.chunk_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec3::child2
evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature
evidence_ledger.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

In summary, this work innovatively employs G2, a solvent that exhibits superior compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the nonflammable phosphate-based electrolyte. This strategy significantly enhances the solvation structure diversity and establishes a G2-dominated configuration, which enables the simultaneous construction of stable (G2-derived) EEIs on both cathode and anode surfaces. These consequently lead to significant suppression of continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigation of TM dissolution, and inhibition of structural degradation in electrode materials. Benefiting from these advantages, PB||HC full cell demonstrates outstanding comprehensive performance, which achieves a high capacity retention of 83.1 % after 300 cycles at 25 °C. Notably, even under the harsh elevated temperature condition of 55 °C, it still maintains 82.5 % capacity after 100 cycles. Additionally, the practical and universal applications are also validated by assembling the PB||HC pouch cells, cylindrical cells and NFM||HC full cells. This work offers new insights into the design of intrinsically safe and long-life electrolytes for next-generation wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries.

evidence_ledger.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

evidence_ledger.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

2.4. Electrochemical performance
To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8. Cells equipped with NTE electrolyte exhibit notably lower charge transfer impedance ( $R_{ct}$ ), such as 974.8 vs. 1249.0 Ω after 50 cycles. This reduction can be attributed to the formation of the robust and conductive interfacial layer on the electrode surface, which facilitates charge transfer and improves interfacial kinetics. Self-discharge tests confirm the superior performance of the NTE electrolyte in Fig. S14, with the full cell exhibiting the CE of 95.2% and a voltage drop of 384.1 mV, both of which are notably improved over the values of 87.7% and 423.8 mV obtained with the NT electrolyte. These findings underscore the enhanced interfacial stability and energy retention of NTE, playing great potential on large-scale energy storage system.

citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

citations.quote:
Ronnie Mogensen, Alexander Buckel, Simon Colbin, and Reza Younesi\*

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

Cite This: Chem. Mater. 2021, 33, 1130–1139

Read Online

ACCESS |

Metrics & More

Article Recommendations

SI Supporting Information

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

Full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes were evaluated at room temperature and 55 °C using the aforementioned electrolytes. The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. The flammability tests indicate that NaBOB in NMP-TMP electrolytes are nonflammable when the electrolyte contains more than 30 vol % TMP.

citations.quote:
NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. The studied electrolytes provided promising long-term cycling in full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes. NaBOB–NMP–TMP electrolytes containing less than 30 vol % NMP are nonflammable and share properties like good ionic conductivity over a wide temperature range while possessing good high-temperature performance and retaining over 50% capacity over 1000 cycles.

![](images/02b845ef0cc752ae9cb076145efdcf41689eb321b41ae3285eab9d31cbe0e36b.jpg)

Freezing point as determined using the $0.1 \, mS cm^{-1}$ temperature as a threshold. Rate capability is described as the percent remaining capacity in the first discharge at 8C as compared to the initial discharge capacity. Cycling stability and high-temperature performance likewise compare the initial discharge capacity with the capacity at cycles 1000 and 100, respectively.

citations.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.quote:
2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

2.4. Electrochemical performance
To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8. Cells equipped with NTE electrolyte exhibit notably lower charge transfer impedance ( $R_{ct}$ ), such as 974.8 vs. 1249.0 Ω after 50 cycles. This reduction can be attributed to the formation of the robust and conductive interfacial layer on the electrode surface, which facilitates charge transfer and improves interfacial kinetics. Self-discharge tests confirm the superior performance of the NTE electrolyte in Fig. S14, with the full cell exhibiting the CE of 95.2% and a voltage drop of 384.1 mV, both of which are notably improved over the values of 87.7% and 423.8 mV obtained with the NT electrolyte. These findings underscore the enhanced interfacial stability and energy retention of NTE, playing great potential on large-scale energy storage system.

citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

Ronnie Mogensen, Alexander Buckel, Simon Colbin, and Reza Younesi\*

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. The flammability tests indicate that NaBOB in NMP-TMP electrolytes are nonflammable when the electrolyte contains more than 30 vol % TMP.

NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. citations.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

的放电结果时，不将缺少同温度、同倍率的循环寿命结果记为阻断缺口。
`unresolved_gaps` 应对应候选组成缺失或用户必需条件，额外研究建议写进验证计划。
若原文已经明写倍率与电流的对应关系，应引用该原句，不将它再次列为缺失。
用户给出的数值与单位须原样保留在至少一个检索查询中，包括括号内的电流或容量。
不能用倍率替换具体电流后就认为已经检索了全部条件。具体标识未命中时先核查
原标识的字面检索结果，再继续扩展候选；不由系统填写论文名称或配方。
在形成候选前，逐项检查用户目标是否已有相关证据。近似温度是选材目标，仍需
优先考察接近该目标的实际测试结果；室温表现不能替代高温或低温使用依据。
近似目标没有容差时不虚构数值阈值。报告必须写出文献实测条件，并在 next_steps
交代目标条件下的验证；不能省略这个目标后把基础配方写成完整解决方案。
成本等定性目标也逐项说明已有依据和待验证事项，不能随硬条件通过而消失。
联合条件的 `electrode` 只写正负极材料，`cell_configuration` 单独写软包、扣式等
电池类型，不把两种信息混写在一个字段中。

## 适用场景

- 用户要求设计适用于特定工况（低温、高压、长循环等）的钠离子电池电解液；
- 用户提供多套候选配方要求评分筛选。

## 证据能力选择

检索查询根据当前用户问题生成，使用英文。先检索用户给出的电极对、电池形式、
温度、倍率或电流及目标性能，不预先限定用户没有指定的盐、溶剂或添加剂。
可把这些条件拆成多个查询，用 `search_literature_multiview` 合并结果；
不必在每个查询中同时塞入所有条件。用户给出的具体电流、容量或电压范围也可用来
定位相关实验，不能只用宽泛的“低温电解液”替代这些信息。
对于有辨识度的电极缩写、明确电流或容量，`resolve_literature_papers` 可补充
字面检索。向量结果未覆盖这些具体标识时，先用原标识检查字面命中，避免继续
围绕不符合电极或电流条件的论文扩展检索。使用用户原本给出的标识，不猜作者或题名。先查看返回的正文命中，
再决定是否值得进行论文内检索；无关的引用、另一种电池的结果不能用于推荐。
找到相关论文后，使用论文内检索分别取得组成、测试条件和性能，核对是否属于
同一配方与同一测试。机理或替代体系检索用于解决实际缺口，不是必做的检索次数。
参数建议：`top_k=10`，`per_query_top_k=8`，`max_per_paper=2`。
盐未指定时，不要只锚定向量检索第一次命中的盐：先用 `kg_query` 的
`find_materials_for_condition`，把 `material_types` 设为 `["SodiumSalt", "Electrolyte"]`，
查目标温度/条件下测试过的盐与电解液，再对返回的具体盐名逐个补向量检索。
双盐体系必须用「dual salt + 具体盐名」组合查询才能召回，单独查一个盐名往往召不回对应论文。
后续查询依据已有结果和 `DecisionState.evidence_gaps` 调整。

## 工作流

### 逆向设计例外：先诊断，筛选仅决定能否推荐配方

对于容量骤降、首圈库仑效率低、高压衰减、阻抗增长等 `inverse_design` 问题，先从检索证据中建立至少两个可区分的电解液侧假设，并提出能区分它们的 EIS、Raman、XPS、LSV、ICP、产气或对照实验。仍执行候选配方筛选，但筛选 `hold` 只禁止“推荐进入实验”的完整配方；不得因此省略诊断、混杂因素和条件化调整方向。报告必须区分“已被证据支持的诊断事实”与“待验证的调整方向”。

1. 解析用户目标与约束；把用户要求的每项条件写成结构化 `constraint_records`，例如：
   不得把整段用户问题放入 `target_conditions`，再把旧文本检查识别到的部分词语当成全部要求。
   推荐前逐项核对用户要求与检查条件，避免漏掉正极、负极、电池形式、温度、倍率或指标定义。
   检索前先解释用户给出的数值条件：它描述什么物理量、单位如何理解、哪些信息尚不明确。
   这一解释依据用户描述的工作场景，在检索前定下，不能由后来检索到的论文或知识图谱记录
   反过来改写；其它论文里恰好出现同样的 “N C” 写法，只说明那些论文的用法，不能用来判断
   用户这句话。
   温度与倍率的单位必须分清。省略度符号的 C 不能直接视为充放电倍率。
   按它在句中的位置判断：直接修饰电芯、电池或其使用环境时（如 “a pouch cell at -30 C”、
   “a full cell around 50 C”），是温度；只有与充放电动作或倍率词连用时
   （如 “discharged at 1 C”、“cycled at 0.5 C”、“1 C rate”），才是倍率。
   按上下文确定一种解释后，就用这一种建立约束，
   不因缺少度符号再补一条互斥的倍率或温度约束，也不因检索结果改回另一种解释。
   检索查询和筛选断言须明确写出所采用的
   物理量与单位。只有上下文确实无法确定物理量时，才同时列出两种解释并说明需要澄清，
   此时暂缓推荐，而不是把两种解释同时写成两条互斥的数值约束。
   接近目标温度的文献结果应保留实测温度，不能改写为目标温度。
   硬约束来自用户问题，不得自行加上某一正极、软包形式、长循环寿命或数值阈值。
   在若干可替代选项之间尚未确定时（例如某类溶剂或某类盐有多种候选），不得把它们
   同时写成必需的 `required_component`；每个选项应作为独立候选分别比较，不叠加互斥的必需组分。
   近似目标也必须进入筛选，不得因用户没有给出容差而省略。保留用户对目标的原话，
   用现有 `evidence_claim` 表达候选须有相应工况下的直接测试依据，而非把近似目标
   改成精确相等、单边不等式或自行设定容差。逐候选判断时，`supported` 须引用该
   候选的实际测试条件与性能原句，`basis` 写清实测条件与目标的差别及其关联依据。
   只有其他工况的结果、测试建议或机理预测时，不能据此判近似工况要求已满足。
   没有相应测试依据就保留 `not_found` 并补证，不能删掉该要求后批准推荐，再把它
   放进 `next_steps`。有邻近条件下的直接依据时，在报告中明确实际条件与目标的
   差别，精确目标下的后续验证可以另列。电极、电池形式和其他明确要求仍须检查。
   联合条件也须保留近似目标的含义：不得把近似值写成 `target_context` 中要求
   精确匹配的数值。近似工况及其电极、全电池归属可写在同一 `evidence_claim`
   中，引用实际共同测试的结果；组分身份等与工况无关的要求不并入该测试条件组。
   “低成本”等定性目标须区分文献提出的成本动机与已量化的价格优势；未提供价格数据
   时不得称已验证低成本。数值明确的用户要求仍按原值建立硬约束，不得因此放宽。
   无法从问题得出数值判据的定性目标，保留为选材目标，在报告中说明依据和待验证
   条件。定性或近似目标通过断言及其原文依据判断，不变成必须命中字面词的关键词条件。
   这不允许省略用户明确给出的电极、电池形式、精确温度或倍率要求。
   当用户目标包含某项性能指标（如 capacity retention relative to room-temperature
   capacity、离子电导率、倍率性能、首圈库仑效率），先分清用户给的是**数值阈值**还是
   **只要报告**：给了明确数值时写成对应数值约束——保持率用 `minimum_retention`、
   电导率用 `minimum_conductivity`、倍率用 `c_rate`，`value` 取用户给出的数值；
   只要求“报告该指标”“有无该结果”而未给数值时，不得把阈值填 0 了事——`value: 0`
   会让任何数字都通过，等于没有检查。这类“须被报告/须成立”的指标改用
   `kind: "evidence_claim"`（见下），把该指标写成一句断言。
   `field_presence` 只用于检查候选的配方字段（`concentration_mol_l`、
   `solvent_ratios`、`additives` 等）是否显式填写，绝不用于表达“某项性能必须被报告”。
   禁止把“capacity retention … must be reported”写成
   `"kind": "field_presence", "field": "additives"` 这类把性能指标错配到配方字段的约束。
   ```json
   {
     "request": {
       "candidates": candidates,
       "constraint_records": [
         {
           "constraint_id": "temp-low",
           "description": "operating temperature ≤ -20°C",
           "kind": "temperature",
           "operator": "<=",
           "value": -20,
           "unit": "°C",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find low-temperature cycling evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "electrode-hard-carbon",
           "description": "hard carbon anode",
           "kind": "electrode_material",
           "evidence_terms": ["hard carbon", "hard-carbon"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find hard carbon anode evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "cell-half",
           "description": "sodium half-cell configuration",
           "kind": "cell_configuration",
           "evidence_terms": ["half-cell", "half cell", "Na||HC", "HC||Na", "pure Na"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find half-cell configuration evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "field-concentration",
           "description": "explicit salt concentration must be present",
           "kind": "field_presence",
           "field": "concentration_mol_l",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": false
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "salt-napf6",
           "description": "NaPF6 as salt",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "NaPF6",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find NaPF6 electrolyte evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "solvent-thf",
           "description": "THF as solvent",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "THF",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find THF solvent evidence"
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```
   定性或断言型要求（如“无集流体/壳体腐蚀被观测到”“无析钠/无枝晶”“提高首圈库仑效率”
   “该添加剂抑制产气”）不得写成 `mechanism_keyword` 关键词表——关键词命中分不清
   “发生腐蚀”与“未发生腐蚀”。改用 `kind: "evidence_claim"`：在 `claim` 里用一句
   用户原话写出对单个候选须成立的断言，在 `claim_verdicts` 里**逐候选**给出判定。
   语义判断（这段原文是否为该候选建立或推翻该断言）由你负责；程序只做两件可机械
   核验的事：判定须指向本次请求的候选，`quote` 须在该候选证据正文中逐字存在。
   因此措辞、否定、同义称呼的变化都不影响判定，你只需如实读原文：
   - `supported`：有原文明确为该候选建立断言，附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `refuted`：有原文明确反驳（如原文说“会持续腐蚀铝箔”），附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `not_found`：检索到的证据未直接提及，如实填写，由补证机制驱动下一轮检索。
   背景介绍、他人体系的结果、无实验支撑的预测都不算 `supported`。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "constraint_id": "no-corrosion",
     "description": "no current-collector or case corrosion observed",
     "kind": "evidence_claim",
     "claim": "该候选电解液不腐蚀铝箔或钢壳",
     "claim_verdicts": [
       {
         "candidate_id": "candidate-1",
         "verdict": "refuted",
         "chunk_id": "fan2024::sec3",
         "quote": "the single NaFSI system can continuously corrode aluminum foil and stainless steel sheets",
         "basis": "原文明确说明单盐 NaFSI 会持续腐蚀铝箔与不锈钢，与该断言相反。"
       }
     ],
     "can_replan": true,
     "search_hint": "find corrosion test evidence for the candidate electrolyte"
   }
   ```
   `evidence_claim` 不得把 `required_evidence_scope` 设为 `component` 或 `background`：
   断言必须由候选自身绑定的证据支持，不能借用别篇论文或背景段落的措辞。
   给出 `supported` 前，逐句核对引文是否真正支持所写断言。引文必须从指定
   `chunk_id` 返回的原文复制，不能把题名、摘要或另一块文字放在该块的标识下。
   配方、测试条件和性能必须对应同一候选；一种优点不能替代另一项目标的证据。
   成本动机与价格比较分别表述，安全性或无氟组成不能自行推导出成本优势。
   `basis` 说明原句与断言的推理关系，不得以重复断言代替理由。程序核验引文
   存在及归属，不代替科学含义判断；证据未支持完整断言时应补证或保留 `not_found`。
   `criteria`/`target_conditions` 仅用于兼容旧调用方；新设计任务必须优先使用
   `constraint_records`，避免 evaluator 再从自由文本猜测硬约束。

   `required_evidence_kinds` 描述的是**支持记录本身的语义角色**，不是实验条件元数据。
   数值性能约束通常只要求 `property`；温度、电极、循环数等共同实例化条件应由该
   observation 的 `condition_scope` 和 `joint_context_requirements` 表达。除非硬约束本身
   确实要求一条独立的 condition 记录，否则不要把同一数值约束写成
   `required_evidence_kinds=["property", "condition"]`，否则会把“带条件上下文的性能观测”
   错当成缺少第二种证据角色。

   当两个及以上硬约束必须在**同一个目标实验上下文**中同时成立时，还必须显式写
   `joint_context_requirements`。分别在多个倍率测试的要求，按倍率分别建立条件组，
   每组的 `target_context.rate` 只填一个倍率。不能把 `0.5 C and 1 C` 当成一次测试的倍率。
   同一论文的不同盐浓度或溶剂比例必须分别对应其性能段，不能因来自同篇论文就互换结果。
   `target_context.cell_configuration` 使用条件检查器的外形名称 `pouch` 或 `coin`，
   不拼成 `pouch full cell` 这样的新标签。全电池要求另用 cell_configuration 检查条件
   和明确的正负极对验证；外形名称不能代替电极与全电池要求。
   它描述的是 evidence composition obligation，不要求所有
   支持证据拥有相同 `experiment_id`。`constraint_ids` 只能引用本次 `constraint_records`；
   `context_fields` 只列对联合决策真正相关的字段；`target_context` 只填写用户明确给出的
   目标条件，未知字段保持未知，禁止为了让 join 成立而补默认值。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "joint_context_requirements": [
       {
         "group_id": "low-temp-high-voltage",
         "constraint_ids": ["retention", "voltage"],
         "context_fields": ["temperature_c", "electrode"],
         "target_context": {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"},
         "can_replan": true,
         "search_hint": "find evidence satisfying both hard constraints at the target operating context"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
   只有约束确实需要共同实例化时才声明 joint group；互不相关的硬约束不要强行合组。
   原文条件检查器分别识别 `electrode` 与 `cell_configuration`。涉及电池形式的用户要求
   使用独立的 cell_configuration 条件；只有相关观测明确提供该字段时，才作联合检查。
2. 检查用户输入与已有 ledger；存在组分、机理或替代体系缺口时，选择相应检索能力；
3. 如证据不足，再做有界补充检索：
   - 区分“已有候选缺少一段证据”和“已有候选并不适合目标”。先检查最相关论文；
     若当前候选仍不能满足目标，按缺口与完整目标检索其他候选，不反复只查原来的
     盐、溶剂或论文。新证据支持新的组成时重新组装候选，再用原任务的全部条件
     筛选。不能把不同候选的成本、工况或性能拼成一个通过的候选。
   - 尚未定位候选论文时，用 `search_literature_chunks` 做 1–2 次聚焦补充（`top_k=10`）；
   - 若返回结果已经给出明确 `paper_id`，且该论文与目标组分/机理直接相关但缺少显式配方或目标工况证据，必须对最相关的 1 篇论文调用一次 `search_paper_chunks(paper_id=..., query=..., top_k=8)`；`query` 用 4–8 个英文技术词描述缺失事实，不含作者名。将结果追加到 `evidence_chunks`，不得跨论文拼接配方与性能。
   - 对 **named-study / named-candidate** 设计任务，在进入 `query_formulation_space` 或
     `screen_formulations` 前，必须先取得同一论文中可追溯的配方/组成证据：至少有一条
     `evidence_kind="formulation"` 的记录能支持候选的盐、溶剂或添加剂组成。只有性能、温度、
     机理 chunk 不能建立候选配方归属；若当前只找到性能证据，应继续检索 formulation /
     composition 段落，而不是手工构造一个 `formulation_evidence_ids=[]` 的候选进入筛选。
4. 用户没有提供可评估候选时，调用 `query_formulation_space`，把目标转成：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","target_conditions":[...],"preferred_salts":[...],"preferred_solvents":[...],"preferred_additives":[...],"excluded_components":[...],"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"max_candidates":3}}`；其中 `evidence_chunks` 必须传入前面检索实际返回、与目标最相关的最多 12 个 chunk，不得只传组分偏好而丢失文献上下文。工具会优先从这些同论文原文块组装候选，再使用 KG fallback；保留工具原样返回的 `candidates`。
   如果候选 evidence 只有 `chunk_id` 而 `text/excerpt` 为空，先调用
   `enrich_formulation_evidence({"request":{"candidates": candidates}})`，并用返回候选
   替换原列表；证据已有原文时不得为形式完整重复调用。enrichment 只补齐原文和元数据，
   必须保留原 evidence 的 `paper_id`、`evidence_kind` 和 `chunk_id`。
5. 若任务涉及离子电导率、温度下的传输性质或需要在多个 NaPF6–EC/EMC/PC 候选之间增加一个轻量定量参考，可在筛选前调用 `predict_formulation_conductivity`。只有以下两种情况允许数值预测：候选已有明确的 NaPF6/EC/EMC/PC 摩尔组成，或调用参数中的 `composition_inputs[candidate_id]` 显式给出 `component_mmol`、`molar_ratios` 或 `x_NaSalt/x_EC/x_PC`。现有 `solvent_ratios` 没有保存 v/v、w/w 或 molar 基准，因此**不得**仅凭“1 M + 1:1”之类字段推导模型输入。含其他盐、其他溶剂或添加剂的候选按域外处理；组成不足时保留 `insufficient_composition`，继续依赖文献/KG 证据。`model_predictions` 与 literature evidence 必须分开：模型预测可以辅助候选比较和后续实验优先级，但不能单独把实验事实型硬约束判为满足。
6. 只有需要形成配方推荐或明确 hold 时才调用 `screen_formulations`：
   传入当前候选和完整的结构化 `constraint_records`。旧文本字段用于兼容历史输入，
   新设计任务不能用它们替代结构化条件。
   每项 `claim_verdicts` 只判定本次 `candidates` 中实际提交的候选。候选集合变更时，
   同步更新各断言的候选判定，保持原任务的全部条件。工具返回参数错误后，修复
   指出的字段并重新提交完整请求，不得删去 `constraint_records` 或联合条件来消除报错。
    倍率与循环次数是两种不同测试，分别建立约束：指定 1 C 测试使用
    `{"kind":"c_rate","operator":"==","value":1,"unit":"C"}`；
    100 次循环使用 `{"kind":"minimum_cycles","value":100,"unit":"cycles"}`。
    指定 2.0–4.0 V 测试使用
    `{"kind":"voltage_window","operator":"==","value":[2.0,4.0],"unit":"V"}`。
    若任务要求 0.5 C 和 1 C，各自建立条件。
    双盐配方同时保存 `salts` 与 `salt_concentrations_mol_l`，分别记录各盐浓度；
    `concentration_mol_l` 表示总盐浓度，不得将它归给某一个盐。
    `solvent_ratio_basis` 按原文填写 `mass`、`volume` 或 `molar`；原文未说明时填
    `unknown`。不得把质量比例当成体积比例，或把溶剂比例直接当成包括盐的摩尔组成。
   若本任务已声明 `joint_context_requirements`，每次首次筛选和补证后的重新筛选都必须携带
   同一份 joint-context 合同；除非用户明确修改任务目标，否则不得在 re-screen 时删除、
   放宽 `context_fields` 或改写 `target_context`。runtime 会在字段被意外省略时保留上一版
   显式合同，但 Agent 仍应主动原样传递。
   保留工具原样返回的 `screening_results`、其中的 `criteria_evaluations` 与 `gaps`，
   不得手写分数、validations 或 scores。任何 `failed`、`insufficient_evidence` 或
   `unsupported` 判定都不得在报告中表述为性能已验证。
7. 旧调用方需要动作列表时，可调用 `optimize_formulations`：
   `{"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results,"request":{"task_type":"design","objectives":[目标性能...],"constraints":[用户硬约束...]}}`。
   不得同时传入 `validations` 或 `scores`。该兼容工具只翻译筛选后已经产生的
   `DecisionState`，不会再按 score 独立裁决；若 proposal 为
   `retrieve_more_evidence`，先执行对应的补充检索和重新筛选，再进入报告。
8. `DecisionState` 已达到 `recommend` 或 `hold` 后，必须**立即**调用 `synthesize_design_report`
   生成完整报告，并传入同一份原始 `screening_results`：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","question":用户问题,"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results}}`。
   为提升 `claim_supported_ratio`，请在 `request.claims` 中提交**所有**被 `evidence_chunks` 直接支持的事实声明（`claim_type="fact"`），每条包含 `text`、对应 `chunk_id` 和唯一逐字原文引文 `evidence_quote`（必须从该 chunk 的 `content` 中逐字截取，且只出现一次）。**禁止为凑数量编造 claim**；若当前证据能直接支持的 claim 不足 2 条，应优先通过 `search_literature_chunks` 或 `search_paper_chunks` 补充检索，最多尝试 2 轮；若仍无法找到更多直接支持，则在报告中明确标注“证据不足”，并只提交已被验证的 claim。报告将渲染“已校验事实”小节，避免裁判从自由文本中抽取不被检索上下文支持的论断。
   报告要让使用者能安排下一步工作。用简明中文分别提交配方组成、文献的测试条件与数值、同条件基准配方的结果，并保留逐字引文。比例需说明质量比或体积比；浓度、添加剂用量不得省略或猜测。文献筛选不能写成新配方已由本智能体实验验证。
   当目标是某项性能时，报告必须包含已检索到的该项性能结果，不能只列出温度、
   电极和电压范围等测试设置。不同盐浓度、溶剂比例和添加剂分支的结果分别绑定到
   其配方。不得借用另一分支较好的结果；保留同一分支完整组成与性能已明确的候选，
   不必强求选取数值最高但组成仍缺失的分支。
   `next_steps` 按本次缺口列出具体核查或实验，包括要比较的配方、温度、倍率、电池类型和测量项目；这些是验证计划，不是已取得的结果。即使为 `hold`，也要展示已取得的候选资料、文献结果和暂缓原因，不得只写状态或检索流程。
   对没有数值判据的选材目标，`next_steps` 也要交代其验证状态。例如成本目标
   需要区分文献的成本动机与实际价格比较，不能因筛选通过就宣称全部目标已验证。
   性能类 `claims` 应优先包含与当前候选直接相连的实验结果，少选一般背景介绍。
   **关键纪律**：一旦 `screen_formulations` 返回 `hold` 或 `recommend`，**不得**再尝试重新构建候选、重新检索或输出自由文本；下一动作必须是 `synthesize_design_report`。若状态为 `search`，最多只做一轮补充检索 + 重新筛选，然后必须进入报告。
9. 直接输出报告全文，不得改写或截断。

## 退出纪律

- 不要求无条件调用所有工具；根据用户已有候选和结构化 evidence gaps 选择能力。
- `synthesize_design_report` 是终端编译能力。调用前必须已有终态 `DecisionState`；
  `search` 状态必须先按缺口补证或换候选，不能用固定工具次数代替状态判断。
- `recommend` 只推荐 approved candidates；`hold` 展示已检索的候选资料与文献结果，说明缺口和验证计划，不推荐或排序候选。

## 候选方案纪律

- 候选配方必须来自 KG 结构化证据或文献 chunk；
- 对于"建议组合"（无完整配方直接实验数据），summary 只写组分和证据来源，不写性能声明；
- 性能/效果声明只能绑定到直接支持该声明的 chunk_id；
- 禁止在"证据摘要"里写入未被任何 chunk 直接支持的推断句；无来源支撑的直接删除；
- **直接回答（direct_answer）只给出候选方案标识和最精简组成**，不要包含"已在某温度验证"、"性能最优"、"最有效"等需要跨证据推断的断言；
- 推荐完整配方必须有原文明确的钠盐浓度。若浓度未知，列为待补资料，不得填入
  “参考基准配方”的浓度并作为已有文献验证的配方推荐。

## 推荐/排序纪律

- 排序理由必须逐条绑定到具体 chunk_id，禁止写"C1/C3/C4 无法满足需求"、"某候选明显优于其他"等无直接对比证据的绝对化断言；
- 无直接对比证据时，只陈述各候选的组分、证据来源与评分，不给出相对优劣结论；
- 对"建议组合"的推荐，只能说明其组分和所依据的证据，不得把多篇证据的性能迁移到该组合上。

## 证据摘要纪律

- 配方段落若讨论多种浓度、多个溶剂比例或不同研究，先定位到单一配方的原文。
  不得把某段的浓度、另一配方的溶剂比例和第三个体系的添加剂拼成候选。
  原文工具返回中的数值、温度符号、配方标识和 chunk_id 应原样沿用，
  不得手工改写成另一温度或用整篇论文的共同身份代替相同测试条件。
- 每条 bullet 必须附带 `[chunk_id]`；
- 禁止输出以"【推断】"开头的句子；
- 禁止把多篇证据的性能迁移到某个候选配方上。

## 引用纪律

- 使用 `[chunk_id]` 格式；
- 禁止引用模型参数知识里的文献；
- 单篇报道就写"某文献报道/某体系显示"，不得升格为普适结论。

## KG 质量反馈

检索或分析过程中，若发现以下可疑情况，**必须**调用 `flag_suspicious_kg_item` 记录，供后续离线人工审查与 KG 矫正；不阻塞当前设计流程。

- **实体标签错误**：如 `ionic conductivity` 被标为 `Additive`，`NaPF6` 被标为 `Solvent`；
- **关系方向/语义错误**：如 `SEI DECOMPOSITION::FORMS::FEC`、明显违背化学常识的关系；
- **属性单位或数值异常**：如电导率 `100 mS/cm` 与上下文矛盾、温度单位混用；
- **同名异义**：如 `TMP` 同时指 `trimethyl phosphate` 与 `2,4,6-trimethylpyridine` 而未区分；
- **证据与 KG 矛盾**：chunk 中的明确结论与 KG 检索结果冲突。

记录时尽量提供：item_type（`entity`/`relation`/`property`）、具体名称/ID、问题描述、触发工具、证据 chunk_id。

## 知识沉淀

设计流程全部结束后，调用 `reflect_now` 进行知识反思和 Wiki 沉淀，
将本次设计的关键结论、发现的知识缺口、改进的检索关键词记录到 LLM Wiki，
供下次相似问题时直接检索复用，减少重复检索成本。

As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability. This work offers new insights into the design of intrinsically safe and long-life electrolytes for next-generation sodium-ion batteries.

messages.content: Excellent — multiple fluorine-free HC||PB candidate electrolytes found. Now let me extract composition and 50 °C performance details from each key paper.

additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Excellent. Now I have several strong leads:

1. **0364_Zhou 2026** — "A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batteries": electrolyte = 1.0 M NaClO4-TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) + 3 wt% VC (NTE), fluorine-free, low-cost, PB||HC full cell, tested at 10–100 °C, at 55 °C retains 100.1 mAh/g after 100 cycles; 18,650 cylindrical cell 93.0% after 50 cycles at 55 °C; also room temp: 81.2% retention after 200 cycles, ICE 82.0%. "around 50 °C" — 55 °C is close. Also PB||HC. This is an excellent candidate. Fluorine-free? NaClO4 (no F), TEP (triethyl phosphate, no F), EMC (no F), VC (no F). Yes fluorine-free. But wait — is it "low cost"? The abstract says "achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance". Good.

   Need to verify the composition details (concentration 1.0 M NaClO4, TEP/EMC 8:2 vol%, 3 wt% VC) — got it from chunk sec4::child2.

2. **0245 (Mogensen 2020, ACS AEM)** — 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP, fluorine-free, low-cost, HC||PW full cell, but room temperature only (conductivity 5 mS/cm at RT). No 50 °C data found yet.

3. **0049_Mogensen 2021** — "A Wide-Temperature-Range Low-Cost Fluorine-Free Battery Electrolyte Based On Sodium Bis(Oxalate)Borate" — NaBOB in NMP/TMP mixtures, full cells with hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes, nonflammable, good high-temperature performance, retaining over 50% capacity over 1000 cycles, wide temperature range. This is highly relevant! Need to check if it has 50 °C data. Let me search within that paper.

4. **0241/0084_Zhang 2026** — fluorine-free flame-retardant TEP + G2 cosolvent, PB||HC full cell, wide temperature 25–55 °C, low cost. Also very relevant. Need composition (salt? likely NaClO4) and actual numbers.

5. **0142_Du 2026** — PBA||HC pouch cells, 50 °C 94.6% after 100 cycles at 1C (that was PBA||Na half-cell), pouch 83.66% after 100 cycles at 0.5C — temperature? Need to check. Uses MP (methyl propionate?) weakly coordinating... need composition and whether fluorine-free. Possibly contains FEC or fluorinated salt.

So the primary candidate set: NTE (0364), NaBOB-TMP/NMP (0049, 0245), G2/TEP (0241/0084).

Note: 0241 and 0084 appear to be duplicate paper IDs for the same paper (Zhang 2026). Interesting.

- 0241/0084_Zhang 2026: electrolyte composition, 55 °C performance.
- 0364: need electrolyte composition details already have; maybe also need the 55 °C data confirmed (have).

Let's search these papers.

Phosphate-based electrolytes typically exhibit poor compatibility with electrode materials, primarily attributed to their inability to form stable EEIs, which deteriorates rapidly at elevated temperature. The unstable EEI induces successive electrolyte decomposition, transition metal dissolution, and structural degradation of electrode materials, ultimately compromising wide-temperature performance $[36–40]$ . Notably, the solvation structure of electrolytes is closely related to the composition of EEIs and significantly influences their stability $[41,42]$ . Owing to their inherent strong coordination ability, phosphate-based electrolyte tends to form phosphate-dominated solvation structures, resulting in phosphate-derived unstable EEI (Fig. 1a, left). In this work, we strategically employ G2 as cosolvent to modulate ion-dipole interactions in fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte. The introduction of G2 fundamentally transforms the solvation structure from phosphate-dominated to G2-dominated, thereby establishing robust EEI at the surface of electrode. The optimized EEI effectively suppresses continuous electrolyte decomposition, transition metal dissolution, and electrode structural degradation, enabling a remarkable improved wide-temperature performance (Fig. 1a, right). This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries.

Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures. Full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes were evaluated at room temperature and 55 °C using the aforementioned electrolytes. The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. The flammability tests indicate that NaBOB in NMP-TMP electrolytes are nonflammable when the electrolyte contains more than 30 vol % TMP.

These consequently lead to significant suppression of continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigation of TM dissolution, and inhibition of structural degradation in electrode materials. Benefiting from these advantages, PB||HC full cell demonstrates outstanding comprehensive performance, which achieves a high capacity retention of 83.1 % after 300 cycles at 25 °C. Additionally, the practical and universal applications are also validated by assembling the PB||HC pouch cells, cylindrical cells and NFM||HC full cells. This work offers new insights into the design of intrinsically safe and long-life electrolytes for next-generation wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries.

Good. Now I have:
- 0049: HC||PW full cells, PRUSSIAN WHITE (Altris AB supplied Prussian white (PW) cathode powder), evaluated at RT and 55 °C. Electrolyte concentration = near saturation (0.66 M for NaBOB in NMP).
- 0364: PB||HC full cells (Prussian blue), 55 °C, 1.0 M NaClO4-TEP/EMC 8:2 + 3 wt% VC.
- 0084: PB||HC full cells (Prussian blue), 55 °C, 2.0 M NaClO4-TEP/G2 6:4 + 5 wt% VC.

Now update todos and build candidates, then screen.

Regarding electrode requirement: the user said "Prussian-white". 0049 explicitly uses Prussian white from Altris. 0364/0084 call it "Prussian blue||hard carbon". I'll be transparent: for 0364/0084 the cathode is described as "Prussian blue" (PBA family) — the user's "Prussian white" is the sodiated form of Prussian blue; I'll note the wording difference in the report and in the claim basis. For the electrode_material constraint I'll accept both terms via evidence_terms (they are the same PBA cathode family), and I'll state precisely in the report each paper's own wording.

Hmm, but honesty about "Prussian white" vs "Prussian blue": Prussian white is Na2−xFe[Fe(CN)6]; Prussian blue is NaFe[Fe(CN)6] (or Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3). Many SIB papers use "Prussian blue analogue" generally, and some use "Prussian blue" loosely for the Na-rich cathode. The 0364 paper is from a group using "Prussian blue||hard carbon"; whether it's sodiated white form is unclear. I'll flag this as a residual uncertainty and put verification in next_steps. And for the verdict basis I'll write it explicitly.

Now let me think about what the evidence_claim verdicts should be.

Claim A (approx temperature): "该候选电解液在硬碳负极||普鲁士白(原文称普鲁士蓝)正极全电池中于接近 50 °C 的目标温度下被实际测试，并报告了该条件下的容量/容量保持结果"

evidence.paper_title: A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batteries
evidence.text: These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$-TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte, 1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

evidence.text: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C.

Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. ... evidence.text: Evaluation of the galvanostatic cycling of the cells cycled at 55 °C points out the NaBOB–NMP electrolyte as the best electrolyte candidate for elevated temperature cycling (see Figure 8a). evidence.text: Electrochemical Cycling. To test the viability of the NMP-TMP solvent mixtures with NaBOB salt as the electrolyte system in sodium-ion batteries, we used full cells with hard carbon (HC) anodes and Prussian white (PW) cathodes. Initial cycling was performed at $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (0.2C) for five cycles; after this, cycling progressed at $150\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (1C) until cycle 52 where a $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ current was used for a single cycle to ascertain the amount of capacity recovery at low current. ... During the first formation cycle at 0.2C, the cells with NaBOB–TMP achieved 73% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) while the corresponding value for NaBOB–NMP was 68%.
