evidence.text: ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). ... Full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes were evaluated at room temperature and 55 °C using the aforementioned electrolytes.

evidence.text: NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. The studied electrolytes provided promising long-term cycling in full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes. NaBOB–NMP–TMP electrolytes containing less than 30 vol % NMP are nonflammable and share properties like good ionic conductivity over a wide temperature range while possessing good high-temperature performance and retaining over 50% capacity over 1000 cycles.

evidence_chunks.content:
These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$ -TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte,

1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec8::child0
evidence_chunks.content: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec8::child1
evidence_chunks.content: As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%. Besides, NTE-based cylindrical cell also demonstrates superior rate capacity at 55 °C in Figs. 5f and S20. Furthermore, the NTE electrolyte maintains robust cyclability in cylindrical cells even at 80 °C, retaining 89.7% of its initial capacity after 50 cycles (Fig. S21). The universality of NTE electrolyte is further validated in full cells incorporating a layered oxide (NFM) cathode. The NTE-based cells consistently exhibit enhanced long-term cycling stability and rate performance at both 25 °C and 55 °C, as substantiated in Fig. 5g, h and S22-S26. These collective findings confirm the universal applicability and superior high-temperature stability of the designed NTE electrolyte.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：candidate-n-tep-g2、candidate-nte。

### 候选资料：candidate-nte（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaClO4；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaClO4：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：TEP, EMC；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=8, EMC=2；添加剂：VC；添加剂用量：VC=3 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec4::child2]：These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$ -TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte,

1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

### 候选资料：candidate-n-tep-g2（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaClO4；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaClO4：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：TEP, G2；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=6, G2=4；添加剂：VC；添加剂用量：VC=5 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec4::child2]：The base electrolytes, $2.0\mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ -TEP+5 wt % VC and $2.0\mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ -G2+5 wt % VC, are denoted as N-TEP and N-G2, respectively. As the content of G2 cosolvent increases, the flame-retardant property of TEP-based electrolyte gradually disappears, where electrolyte with TEP:G2 vol. ratio of 6:4 endows the highest ionic conductivity and nonflammable nature (Figs. S1 and S2). Moreover, $2.0\mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ -TEP/G2 (6:4 vol. %) +5 wt % VC also exhibits the highest reversible capability with stable long-term cycling of PB||HC full cells in Fig. S3, and the designed electrolyte is denoted as N-TEP/G2 in the following. As shown in Fig. S4, the N-TEP/G2 electrolyte exhibits a slightly higher oxidation potential (4.80 V) than N-TEP (4.65 V) in Na||stainless steel cells, indicating its good electrochemical stability.

![](images/23f05a528ba382787cc090dbacc2e889fb19c9d02755bddfd68a4a7b4678e178.jpg)  
Fig. 1. (a) Schematic illustration of the transformation of solvation structure and interfacial chemistry in N-TEP and N-TEP/G2 electrolyte. (b) HOMO and LUMO energy levels of $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ salts, commonly used solvents and additive. (c) ESP density distribution.

## 候选评估
### candidate-nte
评估建议：候选与文献 NTE 电解质配方完全一致，满足氟免、低成本 NaClO4、PB||HC 全电池及约 50 °C（55 °C 实测）等全部科学要求，依据充分，建议推荐。

- 氟免（fluorine-free）电解质：摘要明确称所设计电解质为本质不燃且无氟，候选不含任何含氟盐或溶剂。 [0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0][0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2]

These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$ -TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte,

1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

source_refs.raw_quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

Besides, NTE-based cylindrical cell also demonstrates superior rate capacity at 55 °C in Figs. 5f and S20. Furthermore, the NTE electrolyte maintains robust cyclability in cylindrical cells even at 80 °C, retaining 89.7% of its initial capacity after 50 cycles (Fig. S21). The universality of NTE electrolyte is further validated in full cells incorporating a layered oxide (NFM) cathode. source_refs.raw_quote: To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8.

source_refs.raw_quote:
2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

![](images/d2e597c13eea9ccd69d779e21aa49a13e0be98a940f94ee5e82f33416bebb987.jpg)  
Fig. 1. Electrolyte design. (a) Schematic illustration of the transformation of solvation structure and interfacial chemistry in NT and NTE electrolyte. (b) Calculated ESP $_{min}$ of solvents. (c) Viscosity of carbonate and phosphate ester, including dimethyl carbonate (DMC), EMC, diethyl carbonate (DEC), propylene carbonate (PC), triethyl phosphate (TEP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP). (d) Viscosity, (e) contact angle, and (f) ionic conductivity of NT and NTE electrolyte.

source_refs.raw_quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

source_refs.raw_quote: This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries. Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. Compared with the commonly used ether solvents, TEP endows the lower HOMO energy level, indicating its excellent antioxidant ability; however, it tends to preferentially decompose at anode surface due to its much lower LUMO energy level, forming the unstable TEP-based solid electrolyte interface (SEI). Moreover, the charge densities of atoms are simulated by electrostatic potential (ESP) density distributions in Fig. 1c, where electrophilic sites mainly concentrated on oxygen atoms and nucleophilic sites on hydrogen atoms [31]. In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

source_refs.raw_quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

Additionally, the practical and universal applications are also validated by assembling the PB||HC pouch cells, cylindrical cells and NFM||HC full cells. This work offers new insights into the design of intrinsically safe and long-life electrolytes for next-generation wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries.

source_refs.raw_quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

source_refs.raw_quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.quote:
2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

citations.quote:
2.4. Electrochemical performance
To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8. Cells equipped with NTE electrolyte exhibit notably lower charge transfer impedance ( $R_{ct}$ ), such as 974.8 vs. 1249.0 Ω after 50 cycles. This reduction can be attributed to the formation of the robust and conductive interfacial layer on the electrode surface, which facilitates charge transfer and improves interfacial kinetics. Self-discharge tests confirm the superior performance of the NTE electrolyte in Fig. S14, with the full cell exhibiting the CE of 95.2% and a voltage drop of 384.1 mV, both of which are notably improved over the values of 87.7% and 423.8 mV obtained with the NT electrolyte. These findings underscore the enhanced interfacial stability and energy retention of NTE, playing great potential on large-scale energy storage system.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec8::child0
citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. Electrochemical Cycling. To test the viability of the NMP-TMP solvent mixtures with NaBOB salt as the electrolyte system in sodium-ion batteries, we used full cells with hard carbon (HC) anodes and Prussian white (PW) cathodes. Initial cycling was performed at $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (0.2C) for five cycles; after this, cycling progressed at $150\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (1C) until cycle 52 where a $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ current was used for a single cycle to ascertain the amount of capacity recovery at low current. All the reported capacities and C-rates are calculated from the active material weight of the cathode assuming $150\ mAh\cdot g^{-1}$ capacity. $^{35}$ Note that a minimum of three cells was cycled for each electrolyte formulation to present the variance in the measurements. During the first formation cycle at 0.2C, the cells with NaBOB–TMP achieved 73% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) while the corresponding value for NaBOB–NMP was 68%. These values can be compared to the 83% CE of the first cycle for the cells using 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC, which is included here as a reference.

citations.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

evidence_ledger.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

evidence_ledger.quote: This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries. Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. Compared with the commonly used ether solvents, TEP endows the lower HOMO energy level, indicating its excellent antioxidant ability; however, it tends to preferentially decompose at anode surface due to its much lower LUMO energy level, forming the unstable TEP-based solid electrolyte interface (SEI). Moreover, the charge densities of atoms are simulated by electrostatic potential (ESP) density distributions in Fig. 1c, where electrophilic sites mainly concentrated on oxygen atoms and nucleophilic sites on hydrogen atoms [31]. In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

evidence_ledger.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

In summary, this work innovatively employs G2, a solvent that exhibits superior compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the nonflammable phosphate-based electrolyte. This strategy significantly enhances the solvation structure diversity and establishes a G2-dominated configuration, which enables the simultaneous construction of stable (G2-derived) EEIs on both cathode and anode surfaces. These consequently lead to significant suppression of continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigation of TM dissolution, and inhibition of structural degradation in electrode materials. Benefiting from these advantages, PB||HC full cell demonstrates outstanding comprehensive performance, which achieves a high capacity retention of 83.1 % after 300 cycles at 25 °C. Notably, even under the harsh elevated temperature condition of 55 °C, it still maintains 82.5 % capacity after 100 cycles. Additionally, the practical and universal applications are also validated by assembling the PB||HC pouch cells, cylindrical cells and NFM||HC full cells. This work offers new insights into the design of intrinsically safe and long-life electrolytes for next-generation wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries.

evidence_ledger.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). To test the viability of the NMP-TMP solvent mixtures with NaBOB salt as the electrolyte system in sodium-ion batteries, we used full cells with hard carbon (HC) anodes and Prussian white (PW) cathodes. Initial cycling was performed at $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (0.2C) for five cycles; after this, cycling progressed at $150\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (1C) until cycle 52 where a $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ current was used for a single cycle to ascertain the amount of capacity recovery at low current. All the reported capacities and C-rates are calculated from the active material weight of the cathode assuming $150\ mAh\cdot g^{-1}$ capacity. $^{35}$ Note that a minimum of three cells was cycled for each electrolyte formulation to present the variance in the measurements. During the first formation cycle at 0.2C, the cells with NaBOB–TMP achieved 73% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) while the corresponding value for NaBOB–NMP was 68%. These values can be compared to the 83% CE of the first cycle for the cells using 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC, which is included here as a reference.

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

evidence_ledger.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. 2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

citations.chunk_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

Ronnie Mogensen, Alexander Buckel, Simon Colbin, and Reza Younesi\*

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

Cite This: Chem. Mater. 2021, 33, 1130–1139

Read Online

ACCESS |

Metrics & More

Article Recommendations

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures. Full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes were evaluated at room temperature and 55 °C using the aforementioned electrolytes. The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. The flammability tests indicate that NaBOB in NMP-TMP electrolytes are nonflammable when the electrolyte contains more than 30 vol % TMP.

NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. Electrochemical Cycling. To test the viability of the NMP-TMP solvent mixtures with NaBOB salt as the electrolyte system in sodium-ion batteries, we used full cells with hard carbon (HC) anodes and Prussian white (PW) cathodes. Initial cycling was performed at $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (0.2C) for five cycles; after this, cycling progressed at $150\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ (1C) until cycle 52 where a $30\ mA\cdot g^{-1}$ current was used for a single cycle to ascertain the amount of capacity recovery at low current. All the reported capacities and C-rates are calculated from the active material weight of the cathode assuming $150\ mAh\cdot g^{-1}$ capacity. $^{35}$ Note that a minimum of three cells was cycled for each electrolyte formulation to present the variance in the measurements. During the first formation cycle at 0.2C, the cells with NaBOB–TMP achieved 73% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) while the corresponding value for NaBOB–NMP was 68%. These values can be compared to the 83% CE of the first cycle for the cells using 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC, which is included here as a reference.

citations.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

2.4. Electrochemical performance
To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8. Cells equipped with NTE electrolyte exhibit notably lower charge transfer impedance ( $R_{ct}$ ), such as 974.8 vs. 1249.0 Ω after 50 cycles. This reduction can be attributed to the formation of the robust and conductive interfacial layer on the electrode surface, which facilitates charge transfer and improves interfacial kinetics. These findings underscore the enhanced interfacial stability and energy retention of NTE, playing great potential on large-scale energy storage system.

citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

citations.chunk_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

citations.quote: This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries. Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. Compared with the commonly used ether solvents, TEP endows the lower HOMO energy level, indicating its excellent antioxidant ability; however, it tends to preferentially decompose at anode surface due to its much lower LUMO energy level, forming the unstable TEP-based solid electrolyte interface (SEI). Moreover, the charge densities of atoms are simulated by electrostatic potential (ESP) density distributions in Fig. 1c, where electrophilic sites mainly concentrated on oxygen atoms and nucleophilic sites on hydrogen atoms [31]. In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

citations.quote: This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries. Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. Compared with the commonly used ether solvents, TEP endows the lower HOMO energy level, indicating its excellent antioxidant ability; however, it tends to preferentially decompose at anode surface due to its much lower LUMO energy level, forming the unstable TEP-based solid electrolyte interface (SEI). Moreover, the charge densities of atoms are simulated by electrostatic potential (ESP) density distributions in Fig. 1c, where electrophilic sites mainly concentrated on oxygen atoms and nucleophilic sites on hydrogen atoms [31]. In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

citations.quote:
Ronnie Mogensen, Alexander Buckel, Simon Colbin, and Reza Younesi\*

![](images/a57342fe57dfa9aba2a962fc3d70a611538ff2f76e6f8f1bb320d9168246863e.jpg)

Cite This: Chem. Mater. 2021, 33, 1130–1139

Read Online

ACCESS |

Metrics & More

Article Recommendations

SI Supporting Information

ABSTRACT: Common battery electrolytes comprise organic carbonate solvents and fluorinated salts based on hexafluorophosphate (PF $_6^-$ ) anions. However, these electrolytes suffer from high flammability, limited operating temperature window, and high cost. To address those issues, we here propose a fluorine-free electrolyte based on sodium bis(oxalate)borate (NaBOB). Although lithium bis(oxalate)borate (LiBOB) has previously been investigated for lithium-ion batteries, NaBOB was considered too insoluble in organic solvents to be used in practice. Here, we show that NaBOB can be dissolved in mixtures of $N$ -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and trimethyl phosphate (TMP) and in each sole solvent. NMP provides higher solubility of NaBOB with a concentration of almost 0.7 M, resulting in an ionic conductivity up to 8.83 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature. The physical and electrochemical properties of electrolytes based on NaBOB salt dissolved in NMP and TMP solvents and their binary mixtures are here investigated. The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures.

The results include the thermal behavior of the sole solvents and their mixtures, flammability tests, NaBOB solubility, and ionic conductivity measurements of the electrolyte mixtures. Full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes were evaluated at room temperature and 55 °C using the aforementioned electrolytes. The results show a much improved performance compared to conventional electrolytes of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in carbonate solvents at high currents and elevated temperatures. The proposed electrolytes provide a high ionic conductivity at a wide temperature range from room temperature to -60 °C as NMP-TMP mixtures have low freezing points. The flammability tests indicate that NaBOB in NMP-TMP electrolytes are nonflammable when the electrolyte contains more than 30 vol % TMP.

NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. The studied electrolytes provided promising long-term cycling in full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes. NaBOB–NMP–TMP electrolytes containing less than 30 vol % NMP are nonflammable and share properties like good ionic conductivity over a wide temperature range while possessing good high-temperature performance and retaining over 50% capacity over 1000 cycles.

Rate capability is described as the percent remaining capacity in the first discharge at 8C as compared to the initial discharge capacity. Cycling stability and high-temperature performance likewise compare the initial discharge capacity with the capacity at cycles 1000 and 100, respectively.
